entities.summary:
Aristippus (b. 434 BCE, Cyrene) was a prominent Cynic philosopher of the Classical era, whose ideas on hedonism and the pursuit of pleasure influenced Western philosophy.


Aristippus was born in Cyrene, a major city in ancient Greece, and was educated by the prominent Cynic philosopher Antisthenes. He later traveled to Athens, where he became a student of the Sophist Gorgias and was exposed to the ideas of various other philosophers. Aristippus' own philosophical system, known as Megarian hedonism, was characterized by its emphasis on the pursuit of pleasure and the avoidance of pain. This ideology was seen as a radical departure from the traditional values of ancient Greek society, which placed a high premium on virtue and civic duty.


Despite the controversy surrounding his ideas, Aristippus remained a prominent figure in ancient Greek philosophy, and his school in Cyrene became a center of intellectual activity. The legacy of Aristippus can be seen in the works of later philosophers, such as Epicurus and the Stoics, who were influenced by his ideas on the nature of pleasure and the human condition.


In his own time, Aristippus was known for his wit and his ability to engage in lively debates with his contemporaries. His autobiography, which was later attributed to him, provides valuable insights into the life and thought of this fascinating figure.
